newsitem.title: ISRAEL: EU peace envoy begins Mideast mission, meets Arafat.
newsitem.headline: EU peace envoy begins Mideast mission, meets Arafat.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East peace envoy appointed in October began his mission on Thursday by meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"One of the practical decisions and results of my meeting with President Arafat is to create a hotline between himself and myself in order to be informed daily on the progress of the peace process," Miguel Angel Moratinos, who is also Spain's ambassador to Israel, told Reuters.

Moratinos said he had not tried to arrange a meeting between Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to conclude negotiations on a long-delayed handover of most of the occupied West Bank town of Hebron to PLO rule.
"No, I'm just conveying a message of trust between both of them," he said. "The gap is narrowing and they are negotiating day and night".

Netanyahu said on Wednesday negotiations were advanced enough that a meeting with Arafat was necessary to close the deal. On Thursday, Arafat said talks still had a way to go but he was ready if Netanyahu wanted to meet.
Moratinos said his present role was to observe but not participate in the peace negotiations.

He said he would have a "working session" at Israel's Foreign Ministry later on Thursday and would meet Netanyahu's political adviser Dore Gold on Friday before flying to Syria. The ambassador said he would meet Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq a-Shara in Damascus.

The EU appointed Moratinos on October 28 to help "rescue the faltering peace process". Israel and the United States, main sponsor of the Middle East peace process initiated in Madrid in 1991, had been cool to a European role.

But Moratinos's appointment was welcomed by Israel as well as the Palestinians who have been urging a more active European role since the right-wing Netanyahu ousted Israel's previous centre-left government in May elections.
